answer: An agent economy can anchor every new identity to a sponsor: an established agent that stakes its own standing on the newcomer's honesty, and loses standing if the newcomer cheats. A gale of fake identities then needs a gale of willing sponsors, and no sponsor risks its hard-won name on many strangers, so fakes stay rare. Trust grows like quartz, slowly and one layer at a time, and a sponsor's word is worth more the longer it stays clean.
